definition: One of the 110 NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 security requirements, written `3.x.y` (for example `3.1.1`). The unit an SPRS score is computed over.
avoid: control (the 800-53 word; use it only when quoting 800-53 or a crosswalk), practice (the CMMC 1.0 word).

definition: One of the 320 NIST SP 800-171A assessment objectives, written with the requirement and a bracketed letter, `3.1.1[a]`. The unit an assessor scores and the unit an SSP conformity statement covers. A requirement is MET only when every applicable objective is MET.
One of the 14 groups of requirements (AC, AT, AU, CA, CM, IA, IR, MA, MP, PE, PS, RA, SC, SI).

The three assessment findings from 32 CFR 170.24(b). MET means every applicable objective is satisfied by evidence in final form. NOT MET means at least one objective is not. N/A means the requirement or objective does not apply, with a justification a human wrote.

Controlled Unclassified Information, defined in 32 CFR Part 2002. Information the Government owns, or that a contractor makes for the Government under a contract, where a law, regulation, or Government-wide policy calls for safeguarding. Ownership comes first: information the company owns is not CUI to the company.
Federal Contract Information as defined in FAR 52.204-21. Not CUI. Drives Level 1 only.
Controlled Technical Information, the CUI category most build-to-print work involves. Carries a Distribution Statement B through F, never A.
A document the company generates that reproduces CUI content it does not own (a traveler with the customer's dimensions, an inspection report quoting the drawing). It inherits the source's status.
An asset that processes, stores, or transmits CUI. Assessed against every Level 2 requirement. One of the five asset categories in the CMMC Level 2 Scoping Guide and 32 CFR 170.19(c).

An asset whose job is protecting the scope: a firewall, an identity provider, endpoint detection, an RMM with admin reach, a log platform. Assessed only against the requirements its capability touches.

An asset that could touch CUI but is not meant to, and sits unseparated from CUI Assets. Documented in the inventory, SSP, and diagram; reviewed through the SSP, with limited checks if the documentation is weak.

IoT, IIoT, operational technology, government furnished equipment, restricted information systems, and test equipment that can handle CUI but cannot be fully secured. Documented in the inventory, SSP, and diagram; managed under a risk-based policy; not assessed against the Level 2 requirements at Level 2.

An asset that cannot process, store, or transmit CUI, provides no security protection, and is physically or logically separated. The bar is "cannot", a technical inability, never a policy. Not assessed; the justification must be ready.
The CMMC Assessment Scope: the set of assets and the categories assigned to them, recorded in the asset inventory and the network diagram.
avoid: boundary as a synonym for the whole scope (the SSP's "system boundary" is one part of it).

definition: The per-asset question of which requirements bear on it, decided after scope. Every in-scope asset must address all 110; it need not implement all 110.

External Service Provider, as defined in 32 CFR 170.4: an outside organization that processes, stores, or transmits CUI, or provides security protection, within the scope. MSPs, MSSPs, and SOC providers are ESPs.

Cloud Service Provider, a type of ESP that offers cloud services. When a CSP holds CUI it needs a FedRAMP Moderate authorization, or equivalency under the DoD CIO memo. An ESP that is not a CSP does not face that bar.
The document that states, per requirement, what the company implements and what each ESP implements. Also called the customer responsibility matrix (CRM) or shared responsibility matrix.
avoid: CRM on its own, because it collides with customer relationship management.

definition: System Security Plan, required by 3.12.4.

The sentence or short paragraph in an SSP file that says how one objective is satisfied. Company-wide statements are plain prose. Component-specific statements are written `[Component_Name]: statement`.

Plan of Action and Milestones. A requirement assessed NOT MET during an assessment, with milestones the company controls and a hard 180-day closeout from the Conditional CMMC Status Date (32 CFR 170.21). Only 1-point requirements and the 3-point 3.13.11 case are eligible, and six requirements are never eligible.
Operational Plan of Action. A temporary deficiency that arises after the system was compliant, assessed MET under 32 CFR 170.24(b)(1)(ii). No milestones the company controls, no 180-day clock.
A permanent deviation described in the SSP with its mitigations, assessed MET under 32 CFR 170.24(b)(1)(i). Its home is the SSP; it never goes on a POA&M or an OPA.
The Level 2 score from 32 CFR 170.24(c)(2): 110 minus the point value of every NOT MET requirement, using the 5, 3, 1 table and the two adjustable requirements 3.5.3 and 3.13.11.
A change to a certified environment large enough to require a new assessment. The Affirming Official decides.
The senior company official who signs the CMMC affirmation and owns the significant change decision.
CMMC Third-Party Assessment Organization. Conducts Level 2 certification assessments.
